lead.title: Abbott secures CE mark under IVDR for Cologuard Plus, its at-home colorectal cancer screening test
lead.deck: The stool-DNA test (age 45+, average risk) can launch in select European markets, subject to national pathways and reimbursement. In the US, the BLUE-C cohort (20,000+ participants) showed 95% sensitivity and 94% specificity for colorectal cancer. A market-access signal for non-invasive screening in Europe, with reimbursement the one to watch.

milestone.title: Phantom Neuro implants first participants in the CYBORG study with its Phantom X sensor
milestone.summary: The under-the-skin sensor reads residual-limb muscle activity and turns it into wireless commands for an upper-limb prosthesis. The outpatient implants (about an hour, no general anesthesia) took place at Cabrini Health in Melbourne in an early feasibility study.
milestone.why: First human validation of an implantable muscle–machine interface that does not touch the nervous system: a de-risking step ahead of any regulatory filing. A US company, to follow as a comparable for European connected-prosthetics players.

deal.thesis: EQT and its consortium (including ADIA and CPP Investments) offer €46.50 per share in cash, roughly a 40% premium to the pre-rumor price; some outlets cite €10.8B enterprise value. A bet on take-private European molecular diagnostics: a major valuation comparable for the whole sector.

brefsEurope.title: Medtronic wins CE mark for its Vitalis pacemaker portfolio
brefsEurope.summary: Five pacemakers built for conduction system pacing (CSP), including ReSyncra CSP with AdaptivCSP. The portfolio is not yet cleared in the US, so Europe goes first.

brefsIntl.title: Labcorp to buy Myriad Genetics’ prenatal testing unit for $210M
brefsIntl.summary: Four tests (FirstGene, Prequel, Foresight, SneakPeek) for about $160M of expected year-one revenue, roughly 1.3x sales versus 2.9x for BioReference: a valuation benchmark for diagnostics.

word.definition: A small sensor implanted in the residual-limb muscles that reads their electrical activity and wirelessly relays it to a prosthesis, controlling it more reliably than skin-surface electrodes.

parts.label: Sensor
parts.role: the ear: picks up the muscle (EMG) signal

parts.label: Wireless link
parts.role: the relay: sends the signal to the prosthesis

parts.label: Decoding
parts.role: the translator: turns the signal into hand motion

how.t: The sensor is placed in the residual-limb muscle in a short procedure.
When the patient intends to move, the muscle contracts and the sensor records the electrical signal.
The signal is sent to the prosthesis, which decodes it into motion.

word.why: Prosthesis control is the market's weak point: surface electrodes drift and shift. A stable implanted sensor promises better use and patient retention. Phantom Neuro just reached first-in-human; the remaining risk is clinical and regulatory, with an implantable-device pathway to fund.

startups.name: Phantom Neuro
startups.use: Phantom X under-the-skin sensor; first human implants in the CYBORG study (Melbourne, Oct 2026)

startups.name: Integrum
startups.use: Listed Swedish group (not a startup); e-OPRA implanted-electrode system on a bone-anchored prosthesis, first US patient implanted in an NIH-funded study

startups.name: Esper Bionics
startups.use: Robotic hand driven by muscle sensors; raised $5M (2024) and aims at next-generation sensors, including implantable ones
